scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes” (preprints/Triple-ergodic-averages-with-distinct-integer-slopes-October-4-2026/triple-ergodic-distinct-slopes.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 883a45bc7b95cfaf), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every system satisfying (1.2), every triple of pairwise distinct nonzero integers λ1, λ2, λ3, and every bounded measurable f1, f2, f3 : X → C, the averages in (1.1) satisfy AN (x) −→ 3 Y j=1 Z X fj dµ for almost every x, as N tends to infinity through all positive integers. The exceptional null set may depend on the slopes and the functions.
